title: An unresolved fork: what a drawing does and does not tell us
introduction: An entirely invented A–E topology, with a deliberately unresolved C/D/E fork. This is an independent demonstration, not an empirical organism tree or a required next lesson.
teacherNotes: Original source topology and activity text: 0BSD. C, D and E share the same represented branching point. The file does not resolve a closer C/D, C/E or D/E pair. A polytomy alone does not establish simultaneous divergence or dates. Rotation preserves all three child subtrees; screen positions supply no additional evidence. All five source tips are included, so the C/D/E displayed group is complete for this synthetic source. Adapt this example to discuss the limits of a supplied tree.

rootState.explanation: Explicitly hypothetical root at the supplied serialization origin for this synthetic sample.

basis.evidenceBasis: No empirical evidence. A–E and their relationships were invented as sample data for authoring layouts.
basis.limitations: Does not describe real organisms. The C/D/E split is deliberately unresolved; drawing order does not resolve it.

activities.prompt: Trace C and D toward the declared hypothetical root. Where do they first meet? Does this supplied fork establish that they are closer to one another than either is to E?
Select all descendants of the chosen unresolved fork. Explain what would be missing if you selected only two of them.
The unresolved fork is reversed in the second drawing. Did that resolve any closer pair or provide an evolutionary date?
